posts.cooked:
Let's look a bit more into the new "cards under cards" ruling.

We have a ruling that a card under another card has no text, and that that does not stop destruction response triggers that move under another card.

So let's look at Explosives Wagon.

our ruling on it is that it stays in play to deal its damage, but that ruling is now being altered by the new ruling.

Now wagon can go under Savage Mana and still act.

So we get interactions like:

1.  Is the static bonus to damage still in effect?  That used to be a simple ruling that yes, it was in effect because the card is still in play.  Now the card is still in play, but it has no text, is it still boosting damage?

2.  Is it still a target?  It has no text, it is not a target, right?  So now Environmental Allies, Grease Gun, cards like that no longer affect it.  What about Stun Bolts?  Throat Jab?  They both specify that the Target cannot deal damage, but that target has left play, if a bounty was on the card it would trigger, Wrest would leave play, and effects that affect targets would no longer affect Wagon.

But it is still dealing damage.

I personally find these 2 rulings to be ridiculous, because they create interactions like this as valid play options.

And thematically, What the heck is going on that Haka just ate something, and then it explodes?  that is absurd.  We are in Bugs Bunny territory.

As for using savage mana while wagon was under it  it still acting I would draw from other rulings to say:

1.  Destroying wagon a second time does not affect wagon in any way, is would continue after mana resolves.

2.  The text is in play so mana would count wagon as being destroyed for its damage and add the +1 to the damage. 

3.  The card would remain under mana until it finished its action then go to the trash.

Unless

3.  The card retaining its text retains its status as a target, in which case destruction by savage mana would put it back under savage mana, in which case it would finish its damage effect and remain under savage mana.

posts.name: AlexxKay
posts.cooked:
OK, good arguments that I was wrong about how to handle Omnitron.  I concede that point.

 

MigrantP's comment at #11 seems to me to be supporting my wording at #3: "Cards underneath other cards lose their text as soon as they have finished processing all other effects caused by their destruction (if any)."

 

Regarding phantskipp's suggestion above: "The card retaining its text retains its status as a target, in which case destruction by savage mana would put it back under savage mana, in which case it would finish its damage effect and remain under savage mana."

It seems to me that if a card has its text, then it also has its HP, so would still be a target.  On the other hand, the same ruling that keeps the Explosives Wagon from starting to explode while already exploding (I don't have exact wording, but approximately "Things can only be destroyed once at a time") would seem to me to apply to Savage Mana as well.  That is, if a given card has already been grabbed by Savage Mana during its initial destruction, then Savage Mana cannot trigger that grabbing effect again. 

Hm.  Thinking about this a bit more...  On the third hand, using Savage Mana's power counts up the cards destroyed by the power use.  In this scenario, although EW was under SM, it would NOT be destroyed by SM, because it was already "being destroyed" and couldn't be "double-destroyed".  So at the end of this weird interaction, SM would have destroyed all the cards that had been solidly under it before, but EW would remain under SM.  It wouldn't "go back" under, but it never got to leave in the first place.
